subject.title: Telegram: per-chat lane serialization (isolated ingress) starves messages.queue.collect — same-chat bursts never coalesce

question: Should busy same-lane Telegram spooled updates be admitted into the active follow-up/collect queue, or should Telegram keep strict per-chat serialization and document collect as unavailable for same-chat bursts?
rationale: The source issue is clear, but the permanent behavior crosses Telegram durability/ordering guarantees and core follow-up queue semantics, so automation should not choose the delivery model by itself.

options.title: Design collect-aware Telegram ingress
options.body: Bridge compatible busy same-lane updates into the active collect/follow-up queue while preserving durable spool replay, ordering, and control-lane escape semantics.

options.title: Document the Telegram limitation
options.body: Keep strict per-chat serialization and make the Telegram same-chat `collect` limitation explicit in queue/channel docs.

options.title: Fold into scheduler fairness
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader scheduler-fairness design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/54488 instead of a Telegram-only repair.

recommendation.title: Design collect-aware Telegram ingress
recommendation.body: Bridge compatible busy same-lane updates into the active collect/follow-up queue while preserving durable spool replay, ordering, and control-lane escape semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the most relevant adjacent follow-up ordering and active-run reply-path changes and are the strongest routing candidate for the cross-boundary behavior decision.
